capabilities.name: Google advertising ID (AAID/GAID)
capabilities.plain: A resettable Google ID apps use for ads, which the person can delete, giving apps zeros.
capabilities.meaning: The cross-app join key on Android: install attribution, retargeting, frequency capping. Users can reset or delete it; kids apps must not send it.

android.prompt_ui: None on install; Settings > Privacy > Ads to reset or delete
android.persistence: Persists until reset by person; reset by factory reset
android.revocation: Settings > Google > Ads > Delete advertising ID (Android 12+); opt out of personalization
android.store_policy: Play Ads policy: use the ad ID for advertising instead of other IDs; Families: must not transmit
android.note: Returns 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000 after deletion (Android 12+). No Privacy Sandbox replacement is coming: the Oct 2025 wind-down left the ad ID as the main cross-app identifier.

ios.note: Apple equivalent is the IDFA (mob.ads.idfa).

limits.headline: Can use a resettable Google ad ID to link your activity across apps
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the app or its ad tool starts
can: Join your activity across apps that use the same ad ID
Count installs, show retargeting ads, and limit how often you see an ad
Give a string of zeros once you delete the ID (Android 12 and later)
cannot: Use the ID after you delete it in Settings, Privacy, Ads
Send it to third parties from a kids app
Follow you after you reset it, as the ID changes
Be used on iPhone; the Apple equivalent is the IDFA
limits.differs: Android only. iPhone uses the IDFA, which needs the tracking prompt.

story.what_it_is: A reset button ID on Android that apps and ad networks use to recognize your phone.

marketing.name: Advertising ID
marketing.pitch: A user resettable ID for advertising that you can delete at any time in settings.

story.for_you: You normally do not see it. In Settings you can reset it or delete it, which turns it into a row of zeros and makes ads less targeted.
story.for_makers: It is the main cross app join key on Android: ads show who clicked, who installed and who came back. Makers use it for install attribution, retargeting and frequency caps, and kids apps must not send it.

use_cases.example: You click a game ad, install, and the ad network matches the ID to prove its ad worked.
A game shows a bonus offer to players who came from a certain campaign and who still have the ID.
A shop retargets you with a banner for the shoes you left in the cart.
An ad network caps a user to three views a day by remembering the ID.
A growth team joins the ID in several apps to see how often users switch.
A fraud tool spots a device with many fake installs using the same ID pattern.

story.android_note: Android lets you reset or delete the ID, and Android 13 needs the AD_ID permission.
story.ios_note: iOS has the IDFA instead, behind the App Tracking Transparency prompt.

technical_bounds: Zero value after delete or without AD_ID
Apps for kids must not send it
Wear OS and other form factors vary

legit_uses: Attribution and ads for consenting users

linkedin.how: Play Data safety lists Device or other IDs as collected, and says none is shared with third parties. Privacy policy 1.4 says outside designated EU style countries LinkedIn may collect or rely on others to collect device information such as an ad ID.

history.change: Delete advertising ID in Settings; zeros returned
AD_ID permission declared; missing declaration returns zeros for apps targeting 13+
Privacy Sandbox wound down; ad ID unchanged

capabilities.name: AdAttributionKit re-engagement conversions
capabilities.plain: Measures whether an ad brought an existing user back into the app.
capabilities.meaning: SKAN could only count new installs. Re-engagement attribution lets advertisers measure retargeting without an IDFA.

android.note: No platform equivalent.

ios.api_surface: AdAttributionKit re-engagement via universal link or URL with conversion tag
ios.note: Before iOS 18.4 only one re-engagement window could be active at a time; 18.4 allows overlapping windows through conversion tags.

limits.headline: Can count whether an ad brought you back to an app you already have, on iPhone
limits.user_action: You tap an ad, then open the app you already installed
can: Tell the advertiser an ad led you to reopen the app
Count it without an ad ID
Work with overlapping windows from iOS 18.4
cannot: Name you or give your device ID in the report
Report right away; there are delays
Work on Android; there is no matching feature
Run more than one window at a time before iOS 18.4
limits.differs: iPhone only (iOS 17.4 and later). Android has no equivalent.

story.what_it_is: Apple's way to measure whether an ad brought an existing user back into an app.

marketing.name: AdAttributionKit
marketing.pitch: Measure installs and re-engagement with privacy preserving reports.

story.for_you: You tap an ad for an app you already have and it opens. Apple quietly counts that the ad worked, without telling the advertiser who you are.
story.for_makers: Old SKAdNetwork could only count new installs. Re-engagement lets advertisers measure retargeting campaigns, so they can win back lapsed users without the IDFA.

use_cases.example: A lapsed player sees 'come back and get a free pack' and returning is counted for the campaign.
A shopper taps a sale ad for an app they have and the retailer sees that the ad led to a return.
A promo for a free ride makes a dormant rider open the app, and the ad network gets the credit.
A streaming service measures how many ads brought back cancelled subscribers.
An ad network reports re-engagement conversions in coarse values after delays.
A growth team compares the lift from a re-engagement campaign against a control group.

story.android_note: The Android counterpart for re-engagement was part of the retired Attribution Reporting plan.
story.ios_note: Supported by AdAttributionKit from iOS 17.4.

technical_bounds: Uses the app's open link to carry the tag
Same crowd anonymity limits

capabilities.name: AdAttributionKit (iOS 17.4)
capabilities.plain: Apple's successor to SKAdNetwork that also covers re-engagement and alternative app stores.
capabilities.meaning: A privacy-preserving way for ad networks to measure installs, reopens and re-downloads. Compatible with SKAN postbacks, adds marketplaces beyond the App Store.

android.note: No platform equivalent after Privacy Sandbox Attribution Reporting was retired.

ios.note: Postbacks reach the ad network; a developer can configure a copy of postbacks (docs); country code and configurable windows came in 18.4.

limits.headline: Can tell an ad network an ad led to an install, on iPhone, with delays
limits.user_action: You tap an ad, then install or reopen the app
can: Tell the ad network an ad led to an install, reopen or re-download
Work with alternative app stores
Send a copy of the report to the developer, if set up
Add the country code and set up windows from iOS 18.4
cannot: Give your name or device ID
Report right away or in detail; reports are delayed and coarse
Work on Android; the Android version was retired
limits.differs: iPhone only (iOS 17.4 and later). Android's matching system was retired.

story.what_it_is: Apple's newer privacy friendly ad measurement system, replacing SKAdNetwork.

marketing.name: AdAttributionKit
marketing.pitch: Measure ad conversions, with user privacy built in and support for alternative marketplaces.

story.for_you: You see nothing. Apple sends delayed, noisy reports to advertisers that an ad led to an install, without sharing your name or device ID.
story.for_makers: It tells ad networks which campaign worked while hiding which person did it. It adds re-downloads, re-engagement and alternative app marketplaces, and works alongside SKAN postbacks.

use_cases.example: An ad network checks that a campaign drove 200 installs and gets the answer three days later.
A studio sees which of its ads bring paying players, using a coarse value after the first day.
A retailer measures how many app installs came from a short video ad.
In the EU an alternative app store uses the same kit to measure installs from ads.
A marketing team compares results across ad networks in one report.
Signed reports stop fake networks from claiming credit for installs they did not drive.

story.android_note: Google's matching Privacy Sandbox attribution plan was retired in October 2025.
story.ios_note: Added in iOS 17.4 and compatible with SKAN postbacks.

technical_bounds: Postbacks signed by Apple
Crowd anonymity applies
Dev beta postbacks for testing

history.change: AdAttributionKit launched with the DMA marketplace changes
Developer postback copy and enhanced configuration
Overlapping re-engagement windows, configurable attribution windows and cooldown, country code in postbacks

refs.label: InMobi: AdAttributionKit leveled up with iOS 18.4

capabilities.name: In-app consent platforms (TCF/CMP)
capabilities.plain: A consent screen the developer shows (in addition to the OS prompt) for EEA, UK and some US laws.
capabilities.meaning: Recorded consent decides what ad SDKs may do. Since 2024 Google requires a certified CMP for ads in the EEA. On iOS it adds a second prompt beside ATT, which Italy called double consent.

android.store_policy: Google EU user consent policy; Play Families
android.api_surface: Google UMP SDK, TCF 2.2 strings in app storage
android.note: Consent string stored in SharedPreferences (IABTCF_).

ios.store_policy: ATT remains separate; privacy manifest tracking flag
ios.note: Italy's regulator treats ATT plus a CMP as double consent.

limits.headline: Can show an extra consent screen on top of the phone prompt
limits.user_action: You see a Consent screen the first time you open the app, often in the EU or UK
can: Ask you to say yes or no to ads, analytics and sharing
Store your answer on the phone
Tell its ad tools what you agreed to
Show again later if you change your mind
cannot: Skip the screen when Google needs a certified one for EEA ads
Count as your consent if the answer is not recorded
Replace the phone's own prompt; on iPhone you may see two
limits.reach_label: Your choice, passed to the app

story.what_it_is: The extra consent screen an app shows, for privacy laws, on top of the phone's own prompt.
story.for_you: You see a screen asking you to accept or manage cookies and ad choices in an app, often before the app opens. Your answer is saved and sent to ad partners.
story.for_makers: Laws like GDPR require consent before personal ad data is used. Makers use a CMP so ad SDKs only do what the saved choice allows, and Google requires it for ads in the EEA.

use_cases.example: A news app asks you to consent to personalized ads before showing articles.
A free game shows a consent form at first launch, then loads ads based on your answer.
An ad SDK reads the saved consent string and serves non personalized ads when you say no.
A social app offers separate toggles for ads, analytics and personalization.
A retailer stores your consent so it can prove it asked, for audits.
A product team measures how many users accept and tunes the wording.

story.android_note: Android has no system consent screen. Apps use a CMP.
story.ios_note: On iOS the CMP appears beside the ATT prompt, which Apple allows if it is not misleading.

technical_bounds: Two prompts on iOS
Consent must precede SDK init in EEA

history.change: Certified CMP required for ads in EEA and UK (Jan 2024)
Italy fines Apple over double consent

capabilities.name: Meta (Facebook) SDK and app events
capabilities.plain: Meta's SDK logs installs and in-app events and can send hashed email or phone to match people.
capabilities.meaning: Ties activity to a Meta account for ads. Can send hashed email or phone (advanced matching). Logs events even for signed-out Facebook users.

android.permission: INTERNET; AD_ID; Install Referrer; optional Facebook Login
android.store_policy: Data safety: advertising ID, app activity; Play SDK Index lists the SDK
android.note: Meta Install Referrer (encrypted referrer) lets Meta see install attribution.

ios.permission: NSUserTrackingUsageDescription for advertiser ID; privacy manifest for the SDK
ios.api_surface: FBSDKCoreKit, AEM (Aggregated Event Measurement), Limited Login
ios.note: After iOS 14.5 Meta used AEM on top of SKAN and Limited Login without ATT.

data.metric: App events, advertiser ID, hashed identifiers

limits.headline: Can send your app activity to Meta and match it to your account
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the app opens or you do something in it
can: Send installs and in app actions, such as purchases, to Meta
Match you using a scrambled email or phone number
Record events for people signed out of Facebook
Use Meta's install referrer to see which ad led to the install (Android)
cannot: Track you across apps on iPhone after you tap Ask App Not to Track, within Apple's rules
Show the real email, only a scrambled version
Stay out of ad matching if you never use Meta products; it can still send events
limits.reach_label: Ongoing, tied to a Meta account
limits.differs: Android uses the install referrer and ad ID. iPhone asks for tracking permission, with Meta's own tools as backup.

story.what_it_is: Meta's code library that reports installs and in app actions so Facebook can match them to ads.

marketing.name: Facebook SDK for iOS and Android
marketing.pitch: Add Facebook Login, sharing and app events to measure ads and understand your audience.

story.for_you: You never see it. If you used Facebook or clicked a Meta ad, the app might tell Meta you opened it, bought something or reached a level.
story.for_makers: Meta uses the events to match purchases to ads and to build audiences. Advanced matching can send hashed email or phone, and the SDK can log events even for people signed out of Facebook.

use_cases.example: A game reports 'level 10 reached' so Meta can find more players like your best ones.
A store app reports a purchase so the advertiser sees which Instagram ad drove the sale.
A login button lets you sign in with Facebook and shares your name and email.
Advanced matching sends a hashed email so Meta can join an app purchase to your account.
A dating app counts how many installs came from video ads on Instagram.
Privacy researchers found the SDK sending data before consent in some apps.

risks: Joins app use to your Facebook profile
story.android_note: Android sends the install referrer and the advertising ID to Meta's systems.
story.ios_note: On iOS, SKAN and ATT limit how much Meta can link, but hashed email matching still works.

technical_bounds: Needs consent for ads use under GDPR
Events can be disabled
Privacy manifest and signature required

abuse: Collecting health or sensitive events (FTC and state cases)

history.change: Aggregated Event Measurement for ATT-denied users
Limited Login for Facebook Login without ATT

capabilities.name: Fingerprinting ban and ATT enforcement
capabilities.plain: Apple forbids deriving a device identity from signals to track someone who said no under ATT.
capabilities.meaning: Stops apps and SDKs from rebuilding an ID from IP, model, locale and similar signals after the person refused tracking. It is enforced mainly at App Review and by required reason API gating.

android.store_policy: Google Play Ads policy: use the advertising ID for ads; persistent IDs allowed only for non-ad uses with privacy policy
android.note: Play does not ban probabilistic matching or IP use; Google changed its ad products to allow IP address use in Feb 2025 and the UK ICO criticised the change.

ios.store_policy: App Review 5.1.2(i): no device or user fingerprinting; ATT rules
ios.api_surface: Required reason APIs, privacy manifests, NSPrivacyTrackingDomains
ios.note: Apple states fingerprinting violates the rules even with consent banners. Enforcement is review rejection and, since 2024, required reason API reasons plus blocked tracking domains.

limits.headline: Can't rebuild your identity from phone details after you refuse tracking on iPhone
limits.user_action: Nothing. You said no on the tracking prompt; Apple enforces it in review
can: Use ordinary details for fraud and app function, within Apple's rules
Measure results in groups without naming you
Use IP addresses on Android; Play does not ban it
cannot: Combine IP, model and language to build an ID on iPhone
Hide it behind a consent banner
Use blocked tracking sites after you said no
Pass App Review if found doing it
limits.differs: Apple bans fingerprinting even with a banner. Google Play does not ban matching and now allows IP use in ads.

story.what_it_is: Apple's rule that bans rebuilding a device ID from small clues after you say no to tracking.

marketing.name: App Review Guidelines, Data use and sharing
marketing.pitch: Apps must not derive data from a device to identify a user who declined tracking.

story.for_you: You do not see anything. It is a rule that says: if you tap 'Ask App Not to Track', the app may not secretly follow you anyway using your phone model, language and IP address.
story.for_makers: Makers who use fingerprinting risk rejection. Apple enforces it at App Review and through required reason APIs, so ad networks moved to clearly permitted measures like SKAN.

use_cases.example: An ad network that mixed IP and model to rebuild an ID could see its apps pulled.
A game studio drops a probabilistic attribution tool to avoid a rejection.
A measurement firm limits itself to consented IDs and anonymous aggregates.
Fraud teams may use signals to stop abuse, but not to track people for ads.
A retailer is told to remove a script that built a device profile from signals.
A developer reads the guideline and rewrites its tracker to use only IDFV inside its own apps.

story.android_note: Android has no equal rule, but Google Play bans abusive fingerprinting for ads on kids apps.
story.ios_note: Applied mainly through App Review and the privacy manifest process.

technical_bounds: Review rejection for SDKs that fingerprint
NSPrivacyTrackingDomains blocked at the network layer when ATT is not granted (declared domains only)
Enforcement is largely review time, not runtime

history.change: Apple tells developers ATT cannot be bypassed by fingerprinting
Required reason APIs announced to curb signals used for fingerprinting
Required reason API reasons enforced for new uploads (1 May 2024)

refs.label: Apple News: Privacy updates for App Store submissions
Apple: Describing use of required reason API

capabilities.name: Google Analytics for Firebase
capabilities.plain: Google's free analytics SDK that gives every install an ID and logs automatic events.
capabilities.meaning: Builds an app-level event stream and links it to Google Ads and BigQuery. Also provides the identifiers Google ad products use.

android.store_policy: Data safety: app activity, device IDs; Consent Mode v2
android.note: App instance ID resets on reinstall or data clear.

ios.permission: NSUserTrackingUsageDescription if IDFA, optional IDFV collection
ios.store_policy: Privacy manifest; ATT when linking with ads
ios.note: Can run with IDFV only; Google Signals needs consent.

limits.headline: Can give each install an ID and log your taps and screens for Google
limits.user_action: Nothing. It starts when the app opens and runs while you use it
can: Count sessions, screens and purchases for the developer
Give each install its own ID that resets on reinstall (Android)
Link to Google Ads and BigQuery reports
Run with the developer ID only on iPhone, without tracking permission
cannot: Join you across other companies' apps without your yes on iPhone
Use Google Signals on iPhone without consent
Keep the same ID after you clear the app data or reinstall (Android)
limits.differs: Android gives each install an app instance ID that resets on reinstall. iPhone can run with the developer ID alone.

story.what_it_is: Google's free tool that counts what people do in an app and links it to Google Ads.

marketing.name: Google Analytics for Firebase
marketing.pitch: Free, unlimited event reporting that shows how people use your app and what drives growth.

story.for_you: You never see it. It logs each time you open the app, how long you stay and what you tap, and gives your install a long random ID.
story.for_makers: It builds an event stream per install and links it to Google Ads and BigQuery. Teams use it to find drop off points, test ideas and send audiences to ads, and it is free, so nearly every app has it.

use_cases.example: A studio sees that 40 percent of players quit at level 3, so it makes the level easier.
A retail app tracks how many users add to cart but never pay, then sends a reminder.
A running app measures which workout types people finish and which they skip.
Google Ads uses the events to find similar users and judge which ads bring buyers.
A video app measures play time and tests a new recommendation row.
A team ties crashes to a version using the same install ID and fixes the bug.

story.android_note: On Android it can also use the advertising ID if the app has the AD_ID permission.
story.ios_note: On iOS it respects ATT for IDFA and otherwise uses an app instance ID.

technical_bounds: EEA consent required for ads linking
Data retention 2 or 14 months default

abuse: Merging with Google Ads audiences without disclosure

history.change: Consent Mode v2 signals for ad_user_data and ad_personalization

capabilities.name: Google Ads app campaign measurement
capabilities.plain: Google Play services and the Firebase SDK report installs and in-app events straight to Google Ads.
capabilities.meaning: Google already knows the click, the install and the account. The SDK adds in-app events, closing the loop with no third-party MMP.

android.store_policy: Data safety must mention ad ID, app activity; consent mode in EEA
android.api_surface: Firebase Analytics, Google Ads conversion linking, Play services
android.note: Uses Play Install Referrer and AAID on Android, SKAN and IDFA (if allowed) on iOS.

ios.store_policy: ATT; privacy manifest for Google SDKs
ios.note: iOS conversion modeling and SKAN conversion value mapping inside Google Ads.

fields.name: gclid / gbraid / wbraid
fields.range: click IDs for web and app flows

limits.headline: Can tell Google Ads about your installs and in app actions
limits.user_action: You tap a Google ad, install the app, then use it
can: Tell Google an ad led to an install, using the Play install referrer
Report in app purchases and events back to Google Ads
Use the Android ad ID, or the IDFA only if you allow it on iPhone
cannot: Send the IDFA on iPhone after you tap Ask App Not to Track
Send data you did not generate in the app
Skip Google's own matching; no outside tool is needed
limits.differs: Android uses the install referrer and ad ID. iPhone uses Apple's delayed reports and the IDFA only if allowed.

story.what_it_is: Google counts installs and in app actions straight from your phone, to prove its ads worked.

marketing.name: App campaign conversion tracking
marketing.pitch: Link Google Ads with Firebase to see which ads lead to installs and in app actions.

story.for_you: You tap an ad on Search or YouTube, install the app and play. Google quietly learns that this ad led to your install and, later, to your first purchase.
story.for_makers: Google already knows the click, the Play install and the account, so the SDK only has to add what happens in the app. That closes the loop with no third party tool, and feeds Google's bidding with real results.

use_cases.example: A studio runs an app campaign and sees which ads bring players who spend money in week one.
A retailer measures how many YouTube viewers install the app and buy within a day.
A ride app measures first ride completions after an ad install, to set its bids.
A bank counts approved accounts from ads and bids more for similar people.
Google's automated bidding learns to show ads to people like past buyers.
A growth team sends the same events to Firebase and Ads and compares the two reports.

risks: Joins ad click to in app behavior
Hard to opt out except by device reset
story.android_note: Uses the Google advertising ID and the Play install referrer.
story.ios_note: On iOS, Google uses SKAdNetwork and consented IDs because of ATT.

technical_bounds: Needs Firebase link to Google Ads
Consent signals required in EEA

capabilities.plain: A resettable device ad ID that apps can read only if the person allowed tracking.
capabilities.meaning: A stable cross-app key that joins a person's activity across apps for targeting, frequency caps and install attribution. Without a yes it is all zeros, so apps must fall back to aggregate methods.

android.note: Android's equivalent is the Google advertising ID (see mob.ads.aaid).

limits.headline: Can use your iPhone ad ID only if you tap Allow on the tracking prompt

can: Link your activity across companies' apps once you allow it
Count installs and limit how often you see an ad
Keep using the ID until you change the setting
cannot: Get the real ID after you tap Ask App Not to Track; the app gets all zeros
Ask without the system tracking prompt
Use the ID on Android; Android has the Google advertising ID
limits.reach_label: Follows you across apps, if allowed
limits.differs: iPhone only. Android uses the Google advertising ID, which you can delete in Settings.

story.what_it_is: Apple's advertising ID, a resettable number that apps can read only if you tap Allow Tracking.

marketing.name: App Tracking Transparency
marketing.pitch: Apps must ask permission before tracking you across apps and websites owned by other companies.

marketing.name: Identifier for Advertisers
marketing.pitch: A device identifier that advertisers use for ads, available only with the person's permission.

story.for_you: A pop up asks 'Allow this app to track your activity across other companies' apps and websites?' If you say no, the app gets a string of zeros.
story.for_makers: The IDFA used to be the key that joined activity across apps for targeting, frequency caps and install attribution. Since iOS 14.5 most people say no, so makers moved to Apple's own reports and first party data.

use_cases.example: An ad network that has your IDFA can show you more shoe ads after you looked at shoes in another app.
A game studio matches installs to ads and learns which campaign brings paying fans, but only for those who say yes.
A retailer builds a group of past buyers to show a loyalty offer in other apps.
A growth team measures lifetime value per ad source for the opted in group only.
A fraud filter spots one device with many fake installs by its IDFA.
A social app uses it to find friends who also installed the same game, if you allow.

story.android_note: Android's version is the Google advertising ID, available without a prompt.
story.ios_note: iOS shows the ATT prompt first, and the IDFA is only available after a yes (about 25 percent in industry surveys).

technical_bounds: Zero value when ATT is not authorized
No user-facing reset button on current iOS; Limit Ad Tracking toggle removed
Prohibited in apps rated for Kids Category

legit_uses: Install attribution and retargeting for consenting users
abuse: Joining a profile across apps and sold-on data sets

capabilities.name: IDFV and App Set ID (developer-scoped IDs)
capabilities.plain: A per-developer app ID that needs no prompt but cannot cross to other companies' apps.
capabilities.meaning: Lets one developer recognize the same device across its own apps for analytics, fraud and fair-use limits. Not allowed for ad targeting on Android and not usable for third-party tracking on iOS.

android.persistence: Resets after 13 months of no use or when the developer's apps are all removed
android.store_policy: Play Ads policy: App Set ID for analytics and fraud, not ad personalization or attribution
android.note: Replaces persistent IDs for non-ad uses when the ad ID is zeroed.

An ad measurement tool sees a gap in sessions and cannot record background events until the next open.
A product team sees a spike of users who force stop right after an update and treats it as a quality warning.
A banking app cannot run its background fraud checks after a force stop, so it checks again at next launch.

story.android_note: Force stop sets a stopped state that blocks broadcasts and cancels alarms and jobs.
story.ios_note: Force quit makes iOS discard silent pushes. Some wake ups like VoIP and location can still reach the app.

technical_bounds: Cannot be detected directly
Region monitoring and some modes survive force quit on iOS

history.change: Force quit prevents background fetch and silent push

capabilities.name: iOS background modes
capabilities.plain: Xcode background modes (audio, location, VoIP, Bluetooth, fetch, push) decide what can run while closed.

android.api_surface: Foreground service types as the closest analog
android.note: Android uses FGS types instead of per-mode entitlements

ios.revocation: Not user visible except Background App Refresh

Keep tracking location until the app stops it, if you allowed Always
Wake up for an incoming call or a Bluetooth event
Refresh content now and then when the system decides it is a good time

Choose when fetch and processing happen, since iOS sets the schedule
Run in the background with no capability turned on in the app's setup

limits.differs: Android has no per mode approval. It uses foreground service types and a visible notification instead.

marketing.name: Background execution modes
marketing.pitch: Apple lets developers enable specific background capabilities such as audio, location, VoIP and Bluetooth in Xcode.

story.for_makers: Makers must ask Apple for each mode and show a real need. The list tells reviewers what the app claims to do, and misuse can get an update rejected.

use_cases.example: A music app keeps playing with the phone locked using the audio mode.
A navigation app keeps giving turn by turn voice directions in your pocket.
A workout app records a bike ride route and heart rate while the screen is off.
A calling app wakes the phone for an incoming call using the VoIP mode.
A home app stays in touch with a Bluetooth lock so it can unlock as you arrive.
A multiplayer game uses the audio mode for in game voice chat that keeps going when you switch apps.

Hard to tell which apps run in the background
story.android_note: Android uses foreground service types instead of one entitlement per mode.

technical_bounds: Review rejects misuse

abuse: Abusing audio or location for keep-alive

ios.revocation: Background App Refresh off; Low Power Mode; force quit

story.for_makers: Makers use it to prefetch content and sync data so the app feels instant. They cannot control the timing, so they pair it with push messages for urgent updates.

A notes app syncs your edits to the cloud in the background so another device is up to date.
A store app refreshes your order status so the screen is already current when you open it.
A health app processes a day of sensor data while you sleep and charge your phone.
An ad and measurement tool uses the short window to upload queued events from the day.

story.android_note: Android periodic work has a 15 minute minimum interval.
story.ios_note: App refresh is about 30 seconds. Idle processing runs for minutes when charging.

technical_bounds: No guaranteed timing
Not run after force quit

story.what_it_is: Apps can tell if your phone is saving power, and iPhone shows if background refresh is on.

marketing.name: Low Power Mode

story.for_makers: Makers use it to be kind to the battery, such as lowering frame rate or delaying uploads. Others can read it as a hint about habits, like someone who is often low on charge.

A product team splits crash and speed reports by power mode to find problems only seen when saving power.
A fraud tool notes whether the device state looks normal for the account holder.

story.ios_note: Low Power Mode pauses background fetch and mail. Apps can also see if Background App Refresh is on, off or limited.

technical_bounds: Both are readable with no prompt

history.change: Low Power Mode and isLowPowerModeEnabled introduced

story.what_it_is: Some Android phone makers add extra app killers that stop apps beyond Google's rules.
story.for_you: You may miss alarms, chat alerts or fitness tracking on some brands, even with every setting on. You may be told to dig through battery menus and allow the app to autostart.
story.for_makers: Makers lose reliable alerts and reminders on these phones and cannot detect or fix it with code. They write help pages and in app guides that ask people to whitelist the app.

use_cases.example: A chat app on some phones stops delivering message alerts after the screen is off, so the app shows a guide to turn off the battery manager.

Do this without Always location on Android or iPhone

marketing.name: Region monitoring
marketing.pitch: Apple lets apps watch circular areas and be told when you cross them, to power place based features.

marketing.name: Geofencing
marketing.pitch: Google pitches geofencing as a way to react when a device enters or exits an area around a place.

story.for_makers: Makers get a cheap way to react to arrival without draining the battery. Stores, smart home and delivery apps use it, but it can also build a record of the places someone visits.

story.for_makers: Makers know most users stay on the default, so reach depends on it. Some apps ask people to switch to Unrestricted for reliable alarms or tracking, which also costs more battery.

A glucose monitor companion app is allowed to run freely so alerts for lows are never missed.
A chat app warns that alerts will be late while it is set to Restricted.

A calendar app that adds a reminder at the right minute needs relaxed battery rules to be on time.

story.ios_note: iOS has a Background App Refresh switch per app and Low Power Mode, which is simpler.

Apps whose tasks time out too often can move to Restricted

Run at all if you did not allow Always location

story.for_makers: Makers can rebuild a rough history of movement without keeping GPS on. It supports commute and weather features, and it is also a way to build a long term travel profile.

fields.range: Active, Working set, Frequent, Rare, Restricted, Never

marketing.pitch: Google describes buckets as a way to prioritize resources for apps people use most and limit those they do not.

capabilities.meaning: Overlays power chat heads and screen filters but are the classic tool for tapjacking and fake login screens. Android 12 limits untrusted touches through overlays.

android.prompt_ui: Settings toggle: Display over other apps
android.revocation: Settings > Special app access > Display over other apps
android.store_policy: Play: allowed for core functionality; review for sensitive uses
android.note: Android 12 hides overlay windows during sensitive prompts and blocks touch pass-through above 0.8 opacity.

ios.note: iOS has no cross-app overlay; closest are Picture in Picture and Live Activities.

limits.headline: Can draw windows over other apps on Android if you flip a switch, never on iPhone
limits.user_action: You turn on Display over other apps for this app in Android settings
can: Show a floating button or bubble above other apps on Android
Show a small panel such as a chat head or screen timer
Use Picture in Picture or Live Activities on iPhone as the nearest tools
cannot: Draw over other apps on iPhone; no cross-app overlay exists
Show over sensitive prompts on Android 12 and newer, where overlays are hidden
Pass your taps through when the overlay is mostly solid (above 0.8 opacity)
Turn the switch on itself; you must do it in Settings
limits.differs: Android has this permission, off by default. iPhone has no overlay, only Picture in Picture and Live Activities.

story.what_it_is: Lets an app draw windows on top of other apps.
story.for_you: You may see a floating chat bubble, a screen filter or a recording button that sits above other apps. You have to turn this on in Settings. Bad apps can use it to cover real screens with fake ones.
story.for_makers: Makers use it for chat bubbles, screen recorders, call overlays and accessibility tools. It is also the classic tool for tapjacking, so Google limits touches through overlays.

use_cases.example: A chat app shows a floating bubble for a new message above whatever app you are using.
A game helper shows a small timer or map above a game while you play.
A blue light filter app dims the screen by drawing a tinted layer over everything.
A screen recorder shows a small stop button floating above your apps.
A driver app shows a floating button for the next ride while the driver uses maps.
Banking malware draws a fake login screen over the real bank app to steal passwords.
A tool shows large buttons above apps for people who have trouble tapping.

story.android_note: Uses the Draw over other apps setting, and Android 12 limits untrusted touches through overlays.
story.ios_note: iPhone does not allow drawing over other apps at all.

technical_bounds: Hidden on secure screens
No equivalent on iOS
Sensitive screens (secure flag) block capture

history.change: Untrusted touch blocking and hide-overlay API
Overlay type TYPE_APPLICATION_OVERLAY replaces system alert types

capabilities.name: Picture in picture
capabilities.plain: Lets video keep playing in a small window while the user uses other apps.
capabilities.meaning: A small floating window. Android lets users disable it per app; iOS supports PiP via AVKit.

android.prompt_ui: System enters PiP on action; user toggle per app
android.revocation: Settings > Special app access > Picture in picture
android.store_policy: Play: none
android.note: Android 12 added auto-enter and seamless resize.

ios.note: iPhone PiP since iOS 14.

limits.headline: Can keep a video playing in a small window while you use other apps
limits.user_action: You tap Picture in Picture or swipe home while a video plays
can: Keep a video or call in a small window above other apps
Start the window on its own when you leave the app, on Android 12 and newer
Let you move, resize and close the window
Work on iPhone since iOS 14 for apps with background audio
cannot: Show the window if you turned Picture in Picture off for the app on Android
Run on iPhone without the background audio setting the app declares
Stay up after you close it; you control the window
See other apps' screens
limits.differs: Android 12 added auto-enter and seamless resize. iPhone has had it since iOS 14.

story.what_it_is: Keeps a video playing in a small window while you use other apps.

marketing.name: Picture in picture
marketing.pitch: Developer guide: let users keep watching a video in a small floating window as they use other apps.

marketing.name: Picture in Picture
marketing.pitch: Developer guide: let video keep playing in a floating window so people can use other apps at the same time.

story.for_you: You start a video call or movie, go to another app, and a small window keeps playing in the corner. You can drag it, resize it or close it. It feels like real multitasking.
story.for_makers: Keeps people watching or on a call while they multitask, which raises time spent and fewer drop offs. Makers must turn it on, and on Android you can turn it off per app.

use_cases.example: You watch a show and answer a text, and the show keeps playing in a corner.
A video call shrinks to a corner window so you can open a notes app and keep talking.
Navigation shrinks to a small window so you can check a message and still see turns.
A sports app keeps a live game in a corner while you check scores.
A cloud gaming or streaming app keeps your friend's stream in a small window while you play.
A lecture video stays in view while you take notes in another app.
Ad makers note that PiP can pause or hide ads, so some services limit it to paid plans.

risks: Hidden window may keep camera on
story.android_note: Turn on per app, and users can disable it for any app in Settings.
story.ios_note: Supported for video through AVKit, and for video calls on newer systems.

technical_bounds: User can disable per app
Video playback only on iOS

capabilities.name: Custom URL schemes and app discovery
capabilities.plain: A custom scheme (myapp://) opens an app; apps can probe which other apps are installed.
capabilities.meaning: Used for deep links and to guess which apps the person has. Both systems now limit probing.

android.store_policy: Play: QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES declaration
android.note: Package visibility filtering since Android 11 (API 30).

ios.note: iOS blocks canOpenURL on schemes not declared; limit 50.

limits.headline: Can open another app by its link name and guess which apps you have
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the app starts or you tap a link like myapp://
can: Open another app by its link name
Check up to 50 named apps on iPhone
Guess which apps you use from which ones answer
cannot: Test names it did not declare ahead of time on iPhone
See the whole app list on Android 11 and later
Take over a link that belongs to a verified web link
limits.differs: iPhone allows a limit of 50 declared names. Android 11 and later filters which apps an app can see.

story.what_it_is: Special web style addresses (myapp://) that open an app, and can be used to test whether an app exists.
story.for_you: A button in one app opens another app on a certain screen. You never see the address, but you notice the jump from app to app.
story.for_makers: Old school way to hand people from one app to another with data attached. It is easy to copy and spoof, so Universal Links and App Links replaced most use, but it still powers login and payment handoffs.

use_cases.example: You tap 'Pay with Venmo' and Venmo opens with the amount filled in, then returns you to the store.
The login screen sends you to the Facebook app to approve, then back to the game.
A share button opens the Spotify app on the exact song you picked.
A friend's invite opens a game with a code already typed into the lobby.
An ad SDK tries a list of schemes to guess which apps you have, which both OSes now limit.
Developers test deep links in the simulator by typing myapp://profile/42.

story.android_note: Android lets any app claim a scheme, so Android prefers verified App Links.
story.ios_note: iOS allows only 50 declared schemes to be checked and prefers Universal Links.

technical_bounds: Apple 50-scheme cap
Android visibility filter

capabilities.name: Universal Links and Android App Links
capabilities.plain: Verified web links that open the app directly, proven by a file on the website.
capabilities.meaning: Lets a site and its app share links and attribution params. The click lands in the app with the URL, including any campaign tags.

android.prompt_ui: Link handling toggle in app settings
android.api_surface: assetlinks.json, Digital Asset Links, App Links
android.note: Verified automatically at install; user can disable in Settings.

ios.note: Link Tracking Protection can remove known click IDs.

limits.headline: Can open the app directly from a website link, with the full link and campaign tags
limits.user_action: You tap a web link from that company in a message, email or browser
can: Open the app on the exact screen the link points to
Receive the full link, including campaign tags and click IDs
Skip the Open in app question, once links are verified
cannot: Open from a site that has not proven it owns the app
Keep known click IDs on iPhone when Link Tracking Protection removes them
Stay on after you turn link opening off in Settings
limits.differs: Android lets you switch link opening off per app. iPhone strips some known click IDs from links.

story.what_it_is: Web links that open the right app straight away, because the site proves the app is its own.

marketing.name: Universal Links
marketing.pitch: Link to content in your app so one URL works on web and in the app.

marketing.name: Android App Links
marketing.pitch: Verified links that open your app directly, with no chooser pop up.

story.for_you: You tap a link and your phone opens the app on the right screen, with no pop up asking which app to use. If you do not have the app, it opens in your browser.
story.for_makers: Links carry tags such as campaign names, so makers can tell which ad or email brought you in. They are a reliable way to bring people from the web into the app, where they buy more.

use_cases.example: An email deal link opens the Target app on the product, with the sale price already showing.
A tweet link to a thread opens the X app instead of the browser.
A link to a live game stream opens Twitch and starts the stream right away.
A tournament invite link opens a mobile esports app on the bracket page.
A click on a paid ad lands in the app with campaign tags that tell the advertiser which ad worked.
A booking link in an email opens the airline app on your trip details.
A shared news article opens in the paper's app where you are a subscriber.

story.android_note: Android checks links when the app installs and can open them with no chooser.
story.ios_note: iOS reads the verification file through Apple and can ignore the link if the user long presses and picks the browser.

technical_bounds: Only works for verified domains
Cannot read link history
Domain must host a verification file

linkedin.how: linkedin.com and lnkd.in links open the LinkedIn app. Use of the lnkd.in short domain as a click-logging hop is inferred, not confirmed.

capabilities.name: Cache and temporary storage eviction
capabilities.plain: The system may delete cache and temporary files when storage runs low; other files stay.
capabilities.meaning: Apps cannot rely on cache data staying. Android clears cache dirs and reports a cache quota; iOS purges Caches and tmp when space is needed, and flags files as purgeable.

android.persistence: Cache cleared on low storage or by the user; per app cache quota via StorageManager
android.note: Low storage clears oldest cache first; quota set by the system

ios.persistence: Caches and tmp purged by the system when low; Documents is not
ios.note: Purge happens while the app is not running; Documents and Application Support are kept

limits.headline: Can store temporary files that the system may delete when your storage runs low
limits.user_action: Nothing. The app saves cache files while you use it
can: Save cache and temporary files, such as image thumbnails
Keep them until storage runs low or you clear them
Rebuild them after the system deletes them
cannot: Keep cache forever; Android clears oldest cache first when space is low
Count on cache staying while iPhone is low on storage; it is purged when the app is not running
Lose Documents or Application Support files on iPhone from this purge
Stop you from using Settings, then Storage, then Clear cache on Android
limits.differs: Android sets a cache quota and clears oldest first. iPhone purges the caches folder while the app is not running.

story.what_it_is: The phone may delete an app's cache and temporary files when it runs low on space.
story.for_you: When your storage is nearly full, the phone may quietly wipe cached images and temporary files. You may see an app reload things it had already downloaded. Your saved files stay.
story.for_makers: Makers must treat caches as disposable and rebuild them when they vanish. It lets the phone free space without asking you, and makers should not hide needed files in caches.

use_cases.example: A streaming app loses its cached thumbnails when space is low and downloads them again.
A photo feed app reloads old images after the phone cleared its cache.
A map app re downloads map tiles it used to have stored in cache.
A game re downloads optional textures but keeps your saved game files safe.
A music app keeps your downloads in permanent storage so they are not wiped, but cached previews may go.
A developer tests low storage to see if the app copes with missing cache.

story.android_note: Android clears cache folders and reports a cache quota for each app.
story.ios_note: iOS purges Caches and tmp folders when space is needed and flags files as purgeable.

technical_bounds: Cache is not durable
Free space readings fingerprint lightly

legit_uses: Offline content that can be rebuilt

history.change: System purges Caches when space is needed

refs.label: Apple: Managing storage and purgeable files

capabilities.name: File data protection classes
capabilities.plain: Files are encrypted at rest, and whether an app can read them while the phone is locked depends on a protection class.
capabilities.meaning: iOS has four data protection classes; Android has credential encrypted and device encrypted storage. This decides if background work can run before the first unlock.

android.persistence: Device encrypted storage available at boot; credential encrypted storage only after first unlock
android.note: Boot receivers before unlock see only device protected storage

ios.persistence: Class A complete: locked unreadable; B complete unless open; C until first auth (default); D none
ios.note: Default class is until first user authentication (C); background tasks after a reboot need C or lower

limits.headline: Can keep files locked until you unlock the phone, depending on how they are protected
limits.user_action: Nothing. You unlock your phone as usual
can: Encrypt files at rest on Android and iPhone
Keep files unavailable until your first unlock after a restart on iPhone
Keep some files in device protected storage on Android for use before unlock
Run background tasks on iPhone after restart only with the lower protection class
cannot: Open locked files from a boot task before you unlock, on Android credential storage
Skip protection by default on iPhone; the default is until first user authentication
Share locked files with other apps
Run iPhone background tasks on the strictest protected files after a reboot
limits.differs: iPhone uses protection classes. Android uses device protected and credential protected storage.

story.what_it_is: Decides whether an app's files can be opened while the phone is locked.

marketing.name: Data Protection
marketing.pitch: Pitch: files are encrypted with keys tied to your passcode, and some can only be opened when the phone is unlocked.

story.for_you: Your files are scrambled so that someone who steals your locked phone cannot read them. You may notice that some apps cannot sync until you unlock your phone after a restart.
story.for_makers: Makers pick how strongly each file is protected. Strong protection keeps data safe but stops background work while locked, so they choose per file based on need.

use_cases.example: A chat app protects stored messages so they cannot be read from a locked phone.
A bank app keeps tokens locked until you unlock the phone.
A health app keeps heart data under strict protection while the phone is locked.
A podcast app downloads new episodes in the background and needs a weaker protection class for that.
A workout app must save a run even when the screen locks, so it uses a class that works while locked.
A home app lets a doorbell alert open before first unlock using only non sensitive data.
A forensic tool fails to read files from a locked phone because of these classes.

story.android_note: Uses credential encrypted and device encrypted storage with direct boot.
story.ios_note: Four classes tied to the passcode, from complete protection to none.

technical_bounds: Background tasks after reboot are limited by class

history.change: File based encryption and Direct Boot introduced

capabilities.name: Document picker
capabilities.plain: System file chooser for one document, such as a resume.
capabilities.meaning: The app gets only the file picked. Resumes and CVs hold name, address, employers and sometimes IDs.

limits.headline: Can open one document you pick from the system file chooser
limits.user_action: You tap Upload file, Attach, or Choose resume and pick a file
can: Open the one file or files you choose
Upload or attach the file you pick
Let you browse folders, iCloud Drive or other storage in the system chooser
cannot: See other files in the folder that you did not pick
Browse your files itself; the system chooser does the browsing
Keep access after you quit, unless you grant lasting access to that file
Change the file unless the app is allowed to edit it

story.what_it_is: A system window where you pick one file to give to an app.

marketing.name: UIDocumentPickerViewController
marketing.pitch: Developer guide: let people choose documents from iCloud Drive and other providers without giving access to everything.

marketing.name: Storage Access Framework
marketing.pitch: Developer guide: let people pick documents through the system file chooser, with access only to what they choose.

story.for_you: You tap Upload resume and a system file window opens. You pick one file and the app sees only that one. The app cannot browse the other files in the folder.
story.for_makers: Makers avoid asking for broad file access, which keeps trust high and clears store review. They still get the files people need to complete a task.

use_cases.example: A job site lets you upload your resume from iCloud Drive or Google Drive with one tap.
A bank app lets you attach a photo of a check or a PDF statement.
A chat app lets you share a document from any storage provider.
A video editor imports a clip from the Files app into a project.
A school app lets students submit a homework file.
A game with mods lets you import a level file you downloaded.
An expense app lets you attach a receipt PDF from your files.

story.android_note: Uses the system file chooser, with access only to the picked file.
story.ios_note: Uses the system document picker, with access only to the picked file.

technical_bounds: No access to other files

legit_uses: Upload a resume for Easy Apply

linkedin.how: Job applications and profile resume uploads use a file chooser. Play Data safety lists Files and docs (optional); Apple label lists Other User Content. Exact picker type is inferred.

refs.label: Android: Open files using the Storage Access Framework

capabilities.name: All files access
capabilities.plain: Gives the app access to nearly all files on the device.
capabilities.meaning: Lets an app read and write most user files. Intended for file managers and backup tools; Play requires a declaration.

android.revocation: Settings > Special app access > All files access
android.store_policy: Play: declaration form; only for core file management, backup, antivirus
android.note: Does not reach Android/data on Android 11+.

story.what_it_is: Gives an app wide access to nearly all files on the phone.

marketing.name: All files access
marketing.pitch: Developer guide: a special access for apps like file managers and backup tools that need to manage most files.

story.for_you: You are sent to a special Settings page to turn this on, not a normal pop up. Once on, the app can see and change most files. Only file managers and backup apps should need it.
story.for_makers: Needed by file managers, antivirus and backup tools. Google Play makes developers fill out a declaration and says no for most apps that only need photos or documents.

use_cases.example: A file manager lets you browse every folder on your phone and move files around.
An antivirus app scans every file on the phone for malware.
A backup app copies all your documents and photos to the cloud.
A game mod manager reads and writes other games' folders to install mods.
A coding app on the phone opens project folders anywhere on storage.
A music player scans every folder for audio files.

risks: Can read most of your files
story.android_note: Special app access granted in Settings, and Play requires a declaration.
story.ios_note: iPhone has no such access, since apps can only see their own sandbox.

iOS has no equivalent

android.revocation: Settings > Apps > Permissions > Music and audio
android.store_policy: Play: data-safety disclosure
android.note: Separate from photos and videos.

limits.user_action: You tap Allow on the music and audio prompt, often in a player or editor app

See your music library on iPhone, after you tap OK

use_cases.example: A music player finds and plays songs you stored on the phone.
A podcast or music editor opens audio clips from your phone to mix.
A rhythm game builds a level from a song file on your device.
A transcription app opens a voice recording from your phone to turn into text.
A workout app lets you pick songs from your own files for a run playlist.
A language app opens your recorded pronunciation clips.
An ad firm could learn music taste from file names if an app gave out the list.

story.ios_note: iOS handles this through the media library permission and file picker.

A photo editor opens your gallery so you can edit any picture.
A visual search app lets you pick a photo of a shoe to find a match.

A running app builds a playlist that matches your pace from songs you already own.
A rhythm game turns songs in your library into playable levels.
A DJ app mixes tracks from your library on a virtual deck.
A social app shows your top songs on your profile.
An ad firm could read your taste to guess age, mood and interests.
A car app lets you pick a song by voice from your own library.

story.for_makers: For a password manager this role is the product: it is how its logins show up everywhere without copy and paste. It is also the most trusted job on a phone, because it can see which services you use.

use_cases.example: A password app fills your work login in a banking app, a news app and a browser, all from one unlock.
A manager shows you only the passkey for the real site and warns you that a look alike site has none saved.
You sign back into a game on a new phone and your manager fills the login and the one time code in a single step.
A company rolls out one approved manager to staff phones so every work app signs in the same way.
A family plan lets a parent share one safe login with a child's phone without typing the password in front of them.
Your bank app asks to create a passkey, and your chosen manager stores it and syncs it to your tablet.

story.android_note: Android treats this as a switch in Settings, and you can have more than one provider with one set as the main.
story.ios_note: iPhone lets third party managers act as the system provider, and the user turns them on in Settings under Passwords.

technical_bounds: User chooses provider explicitly in Settings on both OS

history.change: Password manager extensions as AutoFill providers

capabilities.name: DeviceCheck two bits
capabilities.plain: Apple stores two bits per device per developer on its servers.
capabilities.meaning: Lets a developer mark a device (for example, trial used) with 2 bits that persist across reinstall and device wipe; no other data.

android.note: Play Integrity gives verdicts, not storage

ios.persistence: Cannot be cleared by the user
ios.api_surface: 2 bits plus last update month; per developer account; server to server with an Apple key
ios.note: Survives reinstall

limits.headline: Can store two yes or no flags about your device on Apple's servers
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the app's server asks Apple about your device
can: Set or look up 2 bits on Apple's servers for this device and this developer
Remember a device was flagged (for example, a used free trial) even after you reinstall
Learn the month the bits were last changed
cannot: Store anything beyond 2 bits and a date
Share the bits with other developers
See your Apple ID, name or any personal detail
Work on Android; there is no equivalent
limits.differs: Only iPhone has DeviceCheck. Android gives integrity verdicts but no storage.

story.what_it_is: Apple lets an app store two private yes or no flags about your phone on its servers.

marketing.name: DeviceCheck
marketing.pitch: Apple offers two bits per device so developers can remember simple things like a used free trial.

story.for_you: You never see it. It can mean that if you used a free trial once, the app may still know after you delete it and reinstall. You cannot clear it yourself.
story.for_makers: Makers use these two bits to stop people from claiming a free trial again and again, or to mark a phone that abused a promo. It survives reinstall and even a wipe of the device, which is why it works so well for abuse control.

use_cases.example: A music streaming app marks your phone when you finish a free trial so a new email cannot get another one.
A mobile game flags a phone that abused a gift code so the same phone cannot claim it again on a new account.
A dating app remembers that a phone was banned for harassment, so a fresh profile does not slip through.
A store limits a welcome coupon to one claim per phone even after an app reinstall.
An ad network flags a device that produced fake installs, then discounts its traffic.
A bank app marks a phone used in a known scam so later sign ins from it get extra checks.

story.android_note: Android has no exact twin. Developers use Play Integrity and server side checks instead.
story.ios_note: This is Apple only. Each developer gets its own two bits per device, so it cannot link different developers.

technical_bounds: Server only
2 bits max

refs.label: Apple: Establishing your app's integrity (App Attest)

capabilities.name: Request an ID or credential from a wallet (verifier)
capabilities.plain: Asks the phone's wallet for a verified age, name or license, with the person's consent.
capabilities.meaning: Shares only chosen attributes (age over 21, name, address) cryptographically signed by an issuer. Replaces ID photos and upload flows when it works.

android.permission: None; verifier registration with Google Wallet for production
android.prompt_ui: Credential Manager sheet listing wallet credentials; user approves attributes
android.store_policy: Google Wallet verifier terms
android.api_surface: Credential Manager DigitalCredential (androidx.credentials 1.5), OpenID4VP, ISO 18013-7, W3C Digital Credentials API in Chrome
android.note: Android supports mdoc and SD-JWT VC through registry providers; Wallet is one provider.

ios.prompt_ui: Wallet sheet: choose attributes, Face ID
ios.store_policy: Apple entitlement request via Account Holder; verifier agreement
ios.api_surface: IdentityDocumentServices (Verify with Wallet), ProximityReader mobile document reader, Safari W3C Digital Credentials API (iOS 26)
ios.note: iOS 26.1 adds passport based Digital ID; iOS 26.2 adds usageDescription for tailored consent.

limits.headline: Can ask your wallet to prove one fact, such as your age, once you approve
limits.user_action: You tap Verify my age or Verify my ID and approve the wallet prompt
can: Ask the wallet for a specific item, such as over 21, your name, or your license
Receive a signed answer after you approve in the wallet
Use the proof to unlock an age gated or ID gated action
Accept the proof on a web page through the browser
cannot: Receive anything you decline on the wallet screen
See credentials you never added to a wallet
Skip the approval prompt
Keep asking for new proofs without a new prompt each time
limits.differs: Android works through Credential Manager and registered wallets. iPhone needs an Apple entitlement and uses Verify with Wallet.

story.what_it_is: An app asks your wallet to prove one fact about you, like your age, instead of uploading an ID photo.

marketing.name: Digital Credentials API
marketing.pitch: Android lets apps and sites request verified details from a wallet, with a clear consent screen.

marketing.name: Verify with Wallet
marketing.pitch: Apple lets apps ask for age or ID details from Wallet and shows what is being shared first.

story.for_you: You see a sheet that says which facts the app wants, like 'over 21' or your name. You approve with Face ID or a fingerprint and nothing else is shared. No photo of your license is needed.
story.for_makers: Makers get a signed fact from the government issuer, so there is less fraud and less ID data stored to protect. It cuts drop offs from long upload steps. They must request only the facts they need, or regulators and users push back.

use_cases.example: An online liquor store asks if you are over 21 and your wallet answers yes without showing your birth date.
A hotel app lets you share your name and ID for check in before you arrive, so you skip the desk.
A bank opens an account in minutes by taking verified name and address from your wallet.
A game with mature content checks your age band once instead of trusting a checkbox.
A social site proves a new user is an adult before it shows age limited rooms.
A car rental or ride app confirms a valid license from your wallet before it unlocks a car.

story.android_note: Android shows a system picker that lists the wallets that can answer the request.
story.ios_note: iPhone shows its own sheet with the exact attributes and requires Face ID, with state support rolling out slowly.

technical_bounds: Verifier must be vetted; credentials issued by supported states and countries only

history.change: Verify with Wallet in apps and web

capabilities.name: Firebase installation ID
capabilities.plain: A random per-install ID created by the Firebase SDK.
capabilities.meaning: Fresh per app install; many SDKs use it as a first-party ID and link it to other IDs server-side.

android.store_policy: Play: data safety disclosure
android.note: 22-character ID, valid until app data is cleared or the app is uninstalled; deleted if unused for 270 days

limits.headline: Can recognize this one install of the app with a random ID, until it is removed
limits.user_action: Nothing. The ID is created the first time the app connects to the internet
can: Tell one install of the app apart from another with a 22 character random ID
Link usage, crashes and messages to that same install over time
Keep the same ID until you clear the app's data or uninstall it
cannot: Follow you to other apps or other phones; the ID belongs to this install only
Survive an uninstall or Clear data; a new ID is made afterward
Stay alive forever on Android if the app goes unused; it is deleted after 270 days

story.what_it_is: A random ID made for each app install by Google's Firebase toolkit.

marketing.name: Firebase installations
marketing.pitch: Developer pitch: a stable, unique ID for each install of your app, used by Firebase services like messaging and analytics.

story.for_you: You never see it. It quietly lets the app and Google's tools tell your phone apart from every other install, and it resets if you delete and reinstall the app.
story.for_makers: Makers get a free, always available ID to count users, send push notifications and run tests. It lets crash reports, experiments and notifications line up for one install without asking for any permission.

use_cases.example: A game studio uses the install ID to give one phone the same A/B test version of the tutorial every time it opens the game.
A chat app uses the ID as the address for push notifications, so a message reaches the right phone.
A product team counts daily active installs and links crash reports to one install without asking you to sign in.
An ad network links an install to a later in-app purchase so it can tell which campaign paid off.
A store app shows you the same test version of its checkout page on each visit, so results stay clean.
A bank sees ten new accounts opened from one install ID and flags a possible fraud ring.

risks: Can be joined to other IDs on a server
story.android_note: Available to any app that includes Firebase, with no prompt.
story.ios_note: Works the same way on iPhone, created fresh for each install of the app.

technical_bounds: Per-app, not cross-app

refs.label: Android: Best practices for unique identifiers

capabilities.name: Game services sign in (Play Games, Game Center)
capabilities.plain: Signs the player into the platform game account for scores and saves.
capabilities.meaning: Gives a game a stable player ID, display name and friends list. It links gaming activity across titles for the same person.
